title: Kernel fragmentation quarantine and traffic-shaping playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
summary: After a capacity event on 2025-02-16 we observed repeated p95/p99 latency spikes driven by uneven kernel utilization. The scheduler's micro-shard heuristic fragmented work across many low-occupancy kernel instances, increasing context-switching and KV cache churn. This ticket captures the quarantine strategy used in mitigation, the traffic-shaping rules applied, and a durable playbook to prevent recurrence.
impact_details: Between 2025-02-16 03:10 and 2025-02-16 04:45 UTC: 18% of generation requests experienced p95 > 800ms (baseline 220ms). Affected customers: 7 high-usage tenants on dedicated pools; impact included several production degradations and one SEV. Root-suspect signal: sharp rise in kernel_count_per_request and per-kernel microbatch < 4 tokens, KV cache miss rate increased ~6x.
timeline:
2025-02-16 03:05 - capacity surge begins in us-west-2; autoscaler scales up heterogeneous GPUs.
2025-02-16 03:12 - first customer alert: elevated p95 for generation routes.
2025-02-16 03:25 - on-call identified burst of small microbatches and increased kernel churn via traces.
2025-02-16 03:40 - emergency mitigation: enable kernel-quarantine mode for top-affected hosts and apply traffic-shaping to steer new requests to warmed kernels.
2025-02-16 04:05 - p95 improved to ~300ms; continuous mitigation kept service usable.
2025-02-16 05:00 - rollback temporary probe aggressiveness changes and schedule follow-up investigation.
2025-02-18 - this playbook drafted; owners assigned and instrumentation tasks scoped.
root_cause: The scheduler introduced a micro-shard heuristic intended to spread short requests across kernels to increase parallelism. Under sudden capacity changes this heuristic interacted poorly with the runtime's KV-cache warming and kernel coalescing logic, producing many kernels with extremely low occupancy. The consequences were higher context-switching overhead, inflated kernel setup/teardown cost, and amplified KV cache misses — all driving long-tail latencies.
mitigations_applied: Enabled kernel-quarantine flag on affected hosts (prevents speculative routing to recently probed kernels)
Applied short-term traffic-shaping: prefer kernels with occupancy_score >= 0.6 for new sessions
Temporarily reduced scheduler probe aggression window from 30s to 6s for the impacted fleet
Warmed KV caches by replaying recent successful prefixes for pinned kernels on restarted workers

followup_tasks: Evaluate scheduler heuristic variants: coalescing-first, occupancy-weighted-probing, and delayed-probe — decision by 2025-03-08
Design a kernel scoring cache to avoid repeated re-probing of the same kernel candidates across short windows
Formalize a 'fragmentation' signal and add automated incident-based triggers for quarantine and traffic shaping
Coordinate with Dedicated infra team to add host-level guardrails that prevent aggressive micro-shard distribution during autoscale events
testing_plan: Build parameterized synthetic workload that varies: request length distribution, arrival burstiness, autoscale events. Run nightly regression suite against runtime-1.20 with the quarantine feature enabled/disabled and with new occupancy scoring to verify p95/p99 stability. Include perf counters for kernel_count_per_req, avg_microbatch_tokens, and kv_cache_miss_rate.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy quarantine gate behind feature flag to canary group (5% traffic, selected tenants) for 48h. 2) Monitor p95/p99, kv cache miss, and CPU/GPU utilization; abort on any >20% regression over baseline. 3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% over 7 days if stable. 4) Simultaneous release of occupancy_score metrics to Console with dashboard and alerts.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive coalescing reduces latency but can increase peak GPU memory pressure; quarantine reduces exploratory probing which could marginally reduce overall throughput. We prefer predictable tail-latency for customer-facing routes. Long-term fix likely combines occupancy-aware probing with a small scoring cache and stronger autoscale dampening. Ensure changes are backward-compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments.
